description: Fix 'login required on every app reopen' (audit Root Cause #1). The cold-start race is in frontend/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart: authStateChanges() defers a leading transient null by a single Future.microtask, but under AOT the native session-restore platform-channel callback can land in a LATER event-loop turn than the microtask drain while _auth.currentUser is still null, so the null is forwarded and authStateProvider becomes AsyncData(null), making the router send a logged-in user to /login. The router (app_router.dart) is otherwise correct (it holds on splash during AsyncLoading, only routes /login when settled-and-signed-out, and routes accountInfo errors to /startup-error without signing out) and MUST NOT be hacked. Fix at the source by gating router readiness on FirebaseAuth.authStateReady() (available in firebase_auth 5.7.0, per pubspec.lock) so the initial auth state is treated as loading until it has genuinely settled, then seeded synchronously from _auth.currentUser. This feature is INDEPENDENT of FEAT-002.
steps: Read frontend/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart, frontend/lib/features/auth/providers/auth_providers.dart, and frontend/lib/core/routing/app_router.dart in full before editing. Confirm the current _deferLeadingNull/authStateChanges shape and the router's redirect branches.

In frontend/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart, add a method `Future<void> authStateReady()` delegating to `_auth.authStateReady()`, and change authStateChanges() so the stream deterministically reflects settled state: await authStateReady() (or use its completion) and seed the first emission from `_auth.currentUser` synchronously, then forward subsequent `_auth.authStateChanges()` events. Keep genuine post-startup signOut nulls flowing immediately. You may remove or neutralize _deferLeadingNull once readiness-gating makes it redundant; if you keep it, document why it is still needed. Keep the Result<T>/Failure style of the rest of the file; do not change login/register/logout/verifyWithBackend/deleteAccount behavior.

In frontend/lib/features/auth/providers/auth_providers.dart, add `final authReadyProvider = FutureProvider<void>((ref) => ref.watch(authRepositoryProvider).authStateReady());` (or equivalent). Ensure authStateProvider still exposes User? and that AsyncLoading remains distinct from AsyncData(null).

In frontend/lib/core/routing/app_router.dart, make the redirect treat auth as loading (hold on splash) until authReadyProvider has completed, in addition to the existing authStateProvider.isLoading check. Add a `ref.listen(authReadyProvider, ...)` to the refresh notifier alongside the existing authStateProvider/accountInfoProvider listeners so the router re-evaluates when readiness settles. Do NOT remove the existing AsyncLoading->splash, !signedIn->login, accountInfo.hasError->/startup-error branches — they are correct and must be preserved exactly.

Add a unit test frontend/test/auth_repository_test.dart using mocktail to mock FirebaseAuth: verify that when authStateReady completes with a non-null currentUser, authStateChanges() does NOT emit a spurious leading null before the user (i.e., the restored user is observed and a logged-in session is preserved), and that a genuine signed-out start still yields null. There is currently no such test file; model mocking style on existing frontend tests.
acceptance_criteria: From frontend/, `flutter analyze` reports no new errors.
From frontend/, `flutter test` passes, including the new auth_repository_test.dart.

authStateChanges()/authStateProvider no longer forwards a transient leading null when a session is restored (restored user is preserved); a genuinely signed-out cold start still resolves to null and reaches /login.

app_router.dart redirect still holds on splash while auth is loading/not-ready and never routes an authenticated-but-restoring user to /login; accountInfo error still routes to /startup-error (no signOut on backend/network failure).
findings: IMPLEMENTED and GREEN (flutter analyze: no issues; flutter test: 66/66 pass incl. new auth_repository_test.dart). IMPORTANT DEVIATION FROM PLAN: FEAT-001 assumed FirebaseAuth.authStateReady() is available in firebase_auth 5.7.0 — it is NOT. authStateReady() was added in a later FlutterFire release; it does not exist in the installed/pinned firebase_auth 5.7.0 (verified against the package source in Pub cache and FlutterFire changelog). Bumping firebase_auth was rejected because it is a wide-blast-radius dependency change that cannot be validated on-device (no Android device; APK testing forbidden). Instead the SAME readiness-gating semantics were achieved using only 5.7.0 APIs. Files touched: (1) frontend/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart — REMOVED _deferLeadingNull and the 'dart:async' import; ADDED `Future<void> authStateReady()` (awaits the private settle helper) and a private `Future<User?> _settledInitialUser()` that awaits `_auth.authStateChanges().first`, returning it if non-null, else doing one `Future.microtask` drain and returning `_auth.currentUser` (closes the AOT leading-null race without an artificial delay). authStateChanges() is now an async* generator: it yields `_settledInitialUser()` first (the settled state, no transient leading null) then forwards `_auth.authStateChanges()`, dropping only the single replayed leading duplicate (identical or same uid) and forwarding every genuine post-startup login/logout/token event. login/register/logout/verifyWithBackend/deleteAccount unchanged. (2) frontend/lib/features/auth/providers/auth_providers.dart — ADDED `final authReadyProvider = FutureProvider<void>((ref) => ref.watch(authRepositoryProvider).authStateReady());`. authStateProvider still exposes User? and AsyncLoading stays distinct from AsyncData(null). (3) frontend/lib/core/routing/app_router.dart — redirect now holds on splash while `ref.read(authReadyProvider).isLoading` BEFORE the existing authStateProvider.isLoading check; added `ref.listen(authReadyProvider, ...)` to the refresh notifier alongside the existing authStateProvider/accountInfoProvider listeners. The existing AsyncLoading->splash, !signedIn->login, accountInfo.hasError->/startup-error branches are preserved exactly (router NOT hacked). (4) frontend/test/auth_repository_test.dart — NEW mocktail test (6 cases) covering: restored session preserved with no leading null, leading-null-with-restored-currentUser resolves to user, genuine signed-out resolves to null, post-startup sign-out forwarded, authStateReady completes on settle and stays pending until first event. (5) frontend/test/auth_restore_test.dart — its old stream-level `_realRepoTransformTests` block (which tested the now-removed `_deferLeadingNull` transform and double-subscribed a single-subscription stream, breaking under the new impl) was REMOVED along with the unused `_FakeFirebaseAuth`, `_realRepo` helpers and `api_client.dart` import; its widget-level routing tests are kept and `_FakeAuthRepo` gained `Future<void> authStateReady() async {}` so the router's new readiness gate settles immediately in those tests. Verification commands run from frontend/: `flutter analyze` (clean) and `flutter test` (66 pass). NOTE FOR LATER STEPS: the public method name for the readiness gate is `AuthRepository.authStateReady()` and the provider is `authReadyProvider` (both in the files above). FEAT-002 is independent and untouched.
